---
title: Tools
---

`open-eda-file-tools` is one project at one version: a collection of EDA
data-file libraries and their command-line front ends, released together from
a single tag.

| Tool | Library | Commands | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Liberty `.lib` parser, writer, viewer and formatter | `liberty_tools` | `liberty-view`, `liberty-format` | shipped |
| Cell LEF parser and query tools | `lef_tools` | `lef-tools` | shipped (alpha) |
| DEF parser, binary cache and design queries | `def_tools` | `def-tools` | shipped (alpha) |
| VCD toggle-count profiler | `vcd_tools` (reserved) | — | on the way |

Every tool shares the project version (`VERSIONING_PLAN.md`); there are no
per-tool version numbers.

## Adding a tool

1. Create the tool's package in its own directory at the repository root
   (`<name>_tools/`), with a `pyproject.toml` and tests. It is a library of
   this project, not a separate project: it uses the shared version.
2. Give it its own command-line entry points, kebab-case and prefixed with the
   file format it reads (`liberty-…`, `vcd-…`, `lef-…`, `def-…`).
3. If it has a Rust backend, point its `[build-system]` at `maturin` and keep
   its native crate beside the package. Add that crate to the workspace
   `members` in the root `Cargo.toml` and re-vendor the crates
   (`BUILD.md`). A pure-Python tool uses a plain build backend.
4. Add the tool to the table above and to the repository layout section of the
   README.
5. Set the shared project version in its `pyproject.toml` and follow
   `VERSIONING_PLAN.md`; do not introduce a tool-specific version.

## Shared conventions

- Tests live beside the tool they cover: `tests/` covers the Liberty tool,
  `lef_tools/tests/` covers LEF and `def_tools/tests/` covers DEF. Each tool
  directory keeps its own development virtualenv and test suite.
- `BUILD.md` covers the toolchain, `CLAUDE.md` covers the repository structure
  and the invariants a tool must preserve.
- There is one release history for the project: tags in `vYYYY.M.D` form, with
  `.N` appended for a second release on the same day (`VERSIONING_PLAN.md`),
  pointing at commits where every tool is at the released version.
